title: 1967 AHSME Problem 22
statement: For natural numbers, when \(P\) is divided by \(D,\) the quotient is \(Q\) and the remainder is \(R.\) When \(Q\) is divided by \(D',\) the quotient is \(Q'\) and the remainder is \(R'.\) Then, when \(P\) is divided by \(DD',\) the remainder is:

solutions.text:
Substitution gives \[ \begin{aligned} P&=(Q'D'+R')D+R\\ &=Q'(DD')+(R'D+R). \end{aligned} \] The remainder bounds imply \(R'D+R\lt DD',\) so this is indeed the remainder.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Substitute the second equation into the first and isolate the multiple of \(DD'\)
